findings.locus: Lemma 4 and its proof, manuscript pp.7–8 (HAL PDF pp.9–10)
findings.finding: Future-column-dependent centered quadratic forms are not adapted to the stated filtration. The lemma is false for its stated arbitrary leave-one-out matrices. This rejects that proof route; it does not refute Theorem 1 itself.
findings.counterexample: Take M=N and iid entries zeta with P(zeta=0)=1/2 and P(zeta=+sqrt(2))=P(zeta=-sqrt(2))=1/4. Set u_n=|zeta_(1,n)|^2-1 and C_(n)=diag(product_(j!=n)u_j,0,...,0). Trace norm is1 and C_(n) is independent of column n. Each centered quadratic form is product_j u_j, so the absolute averaged form equals1 for every N.

findings.locus: Theorem 1 PDF pp.8–9 and complete Section2 proof PDF pp.12–16
findings.finding: Finite-fourth-moment directional spectral convergence has an adapted resolvent martingale proof, with prior MP/edge and quadratic-form inequalities required. The isotropic population direction condition holds automatically.
findings.local_proof_design_corrections: In (2.6), the elementary stated estimates justify O(N^(-1/2)) after multiplying N, sufficient for convergence. Bound delta3 in (2.8) directly using bounded beta, deterministic bounded C_n and bilinear adapted resolvent concentration; do not drop the correlated b1 term by an unsupported equality.
findings.risk_closure_design: For aspect gamma!=1, a separate nonzero spectral edge gap allows continuous cutoffs for the zero-eigenspace projection and the positive-spectrum pseudoinverse. Directional and ordinary spectral weak convergence then give isotropic bias/variance limits without the rejected Rubio lemma or a derivative exchange.
